general.q: In golf, what is the term for scoring three strokes under par on a single hole?
general.why: An albatross (or double eagle) is three under par, while two under par is an eagle and one under is a birdie.

general.q: Which treaty, signed in 1919, officially brought an end to the First World War?
general.why: Signed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles in 1919, the treaty formally ended the state of war with Germany.

general.q: What is the capital city of Australia?
general.why: Canberra was selected as a compromise capital in 1908 to settle a rivalry between Sydney and Melbourne.

general.q: Which liqueur is traditionally used to flame a classic Crêpe Suzette?
general.why: Grand Marnier, an orange liqueur made from cognac, is ignited to flame the dessert right before serving.

general.q: Which gas in the upper atmosphere of Uranus absorbs red light, giving it a blue-green colour?
general.why: Atmospheric methane absorbs red light, reflecting the characteristic blue-green wavelengths into space.

pop.q: In the BBC comedy Bottom, what is the name of the local pub frequented by Richie and Eddie?
pop.why: Richie and Eddie frequently cause chaos in their favourite local, The Lamb and Flag.

pop.q: Which 1990s toy line featured compact plastic playsets shaped like skulls, designed as a rival to Polly Pocket?
pop.why: Mighty Max was created by Bluebird Toys in 1992 as a boy-oriented counterpart to Polly Pocket.

pop.q: Which meat snack was famously advertised in the 1990s using an aggressive cartoon character voiced by Ade Edmondson?
pop.why: Ade Edmondson voiced the iconic angry stick figure in Peperami's 'It's a bit of an animal' ads.

pop.q: In the 1998 Nintendo 64 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, what is the name of Link's fairy companion?
pop.why: Navi guides Link throughout his quest, famously shouting 'Hey!' and 'Listen!' at the player.

pop.q: In the 1984 film Ghostbusters, what is the name of the demonic Gatekeeper that possesses Dana Barrett?
pop.why: Zuul is the Gatekeeper of Gozer who possesses Dana, famously declaring 'There is no Dana, only Zuul'.

music.q: What was the title of Supergrass's hit debut studio album, released in 1995?
music.why: I Should Coco reached UK Number 1 in 1995 and featured the hit single 'Alright'.

music.q: Which pop group scored a UK Number 1 single in 1983 with 'Karma Chameleon'?
music.why: 'Karma Chameleon' was Culture Club's second UK Number 1 single and the UK's best-selling single of 1983.

music.q: Which rock duo's 2002 music video for 'Fell in Love with a Girl' was animated entirely using Lego bricks?
music.why: Directed by Michel Gondry, the Lego animation for 'Fell in Love with a Girl' won three MTV Video Music Awards.

music.q: Which disco group secured the UK Christmas Number 1 single in 1978 with 'Mary's Boy Child – Oh My Lord'?
music.why: Boney M.'s festive hit sold over 1.8 million copies in the UK, becoming one of the best-selling singles ever.

music.q: Which country won the 2006 Eurovision Song Contest with the heavy metal band Lordi?
music.why: Lordi gave Finland their first Eurovision victory with their hard rock anthem 'Hard Rock Hallelujah'.

mix.q: Which Welsh alt-rock band had a top five UK hit in 1998 with the single 'Mulder and Scully'?
mix.why: Catatonia, fronted by Cerys Matthews, scored a huge hit named after The X-Files characters.

mix.q: In the BBC sci-fi sitcom Red Dwarf, what is the middle name of the hologram character Arnold Rimmer?
mix.why: Arnold Judas Rimmer frequently complains about his unfortunate middle name.

mix.q: Which river is the longest contained entirely within the borders of Scotland?
mix.why: The River Tay flows for 117 miles, making it the longest river entirely in Scotland.

mix.q: Which English pop band released the smash-hit 1982 album 'Rio', featuring 'Hungry Like the Wolf'?
mix.why: Duran Duran's second studio album spent 110 weeks on the UK Albums Chart.

mix.q: Which actress won an Academy Award for playing police chief Marge Gunderson in the 1996 film Fargo?
mix.why: Frances McDormand won Best Actress for her iconic portrayal of the pregnant police chief.

mix.q: What is the largest organ in the human body by surface area and mass?
mix.why: The skin covers approximately two square metres on an average adult.

mix.q: Which French electronic music duo released the hit 2001 album 'Discovery', featuring 'One More Time'?
mix.why: Daft Punk released Discovery in 2001, which later formed the soundtrack to Interstella 5555.

mix.q: Which flagship sci-fi video game franchise features the protagonist Master Chief?
mix.why: Master Chief first appeared in Halo: Combat Evolved on the original Xbox in 2001.

mix.q: Which espresso-based coffee drink is prepared by diluting a shot of espresso with hot water?
mix.why: The Americano got its name when American soldiers in WWII diluted Italian espresso with hot water.

mix.q: Which Scottish band released the hit 1999 album 'The Man Who', featuring 'Why Does It Always Rain on Me?'?
mix.why: Travis achieved huge commercial success in 1999 with their second album, The Man Who.
